reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) directly supports the key premises: it shows that a 10.2 at.% Al coating had the best corrosion resistance and minimum oxygen penetration due to a denser oxide layer of Nb2Zr6O17 and ZrO2, and that the coating was deposited on Zr-alloy by the stated method. The hypothesis accurately represents these findings, though the evidence is from a single study and the LOCA-specific condition is an extrapolation.
premises: AlNbTiZr MEA coatings with ~10 at.% Al form a denser oxide layer than coatings with other Al contents
The denser oxide layer consists of protective phases such as Nb2Zr6O17 and ZrO2
The denser oxide layer limits oxygen diffusion, reducing oxygen penetration depth
The coating can be deposited on Zr-alloy cladding by RF magnetron co-sputtering
The improvement is specific to high-temperature steam oxidation (LOCA) conditions
